text: {"frames":["Tolling came up out of the fog, slow and wet, from the bell of the village that sank under the polder long ago. Edith, the learned owl from the mill, had bet you a jar of herring that the bell only rang when someone was lying. You climbed the wooden stairs, where the mill wheel groaned and spat drops of water, and found the bell rope already swinging by itself. Edith blinked her round yellow eyes and said the bell would stop once someone counted what the Tower owed it. The bell was owed a share of every hundred, and the rope waited for your answer. What percentage is 0.59?","\"Nobody has ever seen him by day,\" said Gareth, holding up a jar of fog that hummed against the glass. She had caught it on the dyke at dusk, where the silent watchman walks his round in wooden clogs that make no sound at all. Tonight the jar cracked, and a grey thread crawled out and pointed toward the lowest floor of the Tower. You followed it along the canal, past a tulip field gone blue in the mist, to a sluice where the water stood as still as milk. The watchman's lantern burned there, and beside it lay a wager scratched in chalk. What percentage is 0.59?","Halfway up the crooked house, the hoist beam let go of its wheel of cheese, which splashed into the canal and rolled off laughing. Every window of the house glowed gold, though the cheese maker had gone home hours ago and the rooms were empty. Pieter, who sells waffles at the market, swore he had seen a shadow in the top window pull a cord. You pulled on the beam yourself and felt it tug back, as if somebody on the other side wanted you to lose your grip. The glow flickered in the shape of a sum, and the windows seemed to wait for you to finish it. What percentage is 0.59?","A blue lantern came bounding over the ice of the frozen canal, and Nell ran after it in her red woollen socks. Behind them the Tower clock struck thirteen, a stroke that no clock in Misty Ford has ever owned. The lantern dived under the bridge, spun twice round a windmill sail, and stopped dead on the top step of the Tower. Nell pressed her nose to the cold glass of the clock face, where the hands had gone wobbly and ran backwards. The lantern bobbed and blinked, and it seemed to want you to say how big the hour really was. What percentage is 0.59?","Luuk, who keeps the sluice gates of the Tower, wanted one thing more than anything: to read the end of the book before the ice melted. The book sat open on a wooden lectern, and its pages filled with ink as slowly as frost creeps over a window. Every time Luuk turned a page, the next line had already written itself, cheerful and a little bit mean. He tapped the margin with a wet finger, and the letters stopped in a tidy row of numbers. The book was waiting for you to write the answer, so it could finish the story. What percentage is 0.59?"]}
